why: Closed-form buoyant ease plus a curve exporter make a stalled move checkable in seconds instead of guessed at.
note: Constants are our own reading of the write-up (bob 0.03). inspect.mjs had no plot subcommand when checked; JSON shape is {name,fps,unit,startFrame,values[]}, whoever adds plot should read that.

why: Exit acceleration and entry decay in px per 60-fps frame, converted to the comp fps, give a real velocity handoff presentation for TransitionSeries.
note: Numbers are the source author's claim. Verified by stills: cut frame blurred and sliding, entry brakes. Entry ends with a small residual speed (about 2.6 px per 60-fps frame) with the 18-frame entry.

why: Only the occluder cut (A) was small and clean enough; it is built as a neutral soft band with drag and settle.
note: Line carry (D) needs the scenes to draw the line, impact slam (B) and light leak (C) conflict with the no-glow, one-accent rules: deferred or rejected in this library.

why: A vw ramp with an enforced text floor stops hero type collapsing into web layout and is additive to the px scale.
note: claim set to 6.5 vw (source 6 to 9) so five words fit the safe area; one accent per frame stays a documented review rule, not enforced in code.

why: Fragment chains in build or replace mode plus a word-budget lint give a checkable answer to text walls.
note: Build mode measures widths with a canvas (needs the loaded font). Recipes (cliffhanger cut, stem plus slot) are prose in the skills, not code.

why: Frame-arithmetic traps are cheap to state and each causes a visible defect.
note: Written as a header comment plus softFade and exitOpacity helpers; the skill-side determinism.md part belongs to another owner.

why: The speed table integrated into position and the log-space zoom are small pure helpers that keep a glide from surging or stopping.
note: The optical-flow check is not built (needs ffmpeg or OpenCV tooling outside studio/).

why: Subframe blur needs a dependency, so it is documented and not added.
note: @remotion/motion-blur 4.0.537 exists (MIT, about 24 KB), unvetted and not installed; velocityCut uses a cheap SVG directional blur instead.

why: Keeping untyped characters transparent in the same flow locks the layout with no measurement.
note: Verified by stills: two-line box and accent rule stay fixed while typing. No cursor by design.

why: A max page time and a sentence break on top of the word cap stop pause-free cut audio from producing a giant page.
note: Opt-in props maxPageMs and breakOnSentence, defaults keep old behaviour; not tested against real cut audio.

why: Same idea as F-A3: sampleCurve, velocityOf and longestStall exist to find a velocity dip.
note: Covers code-side sampling only; scenes with several animated values need their own sampleCurve call.
